name: drone-draft
about: A draft for a drone pack: the types and the grid of a small quadcopter with four like rotor sets on four like arms, one battery and a frame of two cut plates. It is written by hand from makers' data sheets, from open papers and notes for the physics, from 14 CFR Parts 107 and 89 and Regulation (EU) 2019/945, and from lists of failure mechanisms and of the stages of a product's life. Each line names one source that raises it, with the page's address and the day it was fetched in the anchor's standard. Other sources give other numbers for many lines. It has no rows and no rules, so every line that can arise is open. Five things are bent to fit the format. One part stands for each set of like parts, and the quadcopter states their number. The quadcopter joins every part itself, because a joined part joins nothing. A rotor set holds two points of its maker's test and not the curve. A part has a field only where a line reads it, so a plate has no thickness here. A position is measured from the rear end of the bottom plate, because a quantity is more than zero. Three things cannot be written by a design yet: a speed of rotation, a charge and a speed have no unit. It is a task for two transcribers and is in no deck that ships.

types.what: four like rotor sets at the corners of a square, each on a like arm and each with its own speed controller, with one battery, one flight controller and a frame of two plates. Two rotors that face each other across the square turn one way and the other two the other way. It has no payload of its own, no folding arm, no pair of rotors on one axis, no tilted rotor and no wing
